Writes a text files with pymol scripts to list significant peptides

Source: R/pymol_script_significant_peptide.R
pymol_script_significant_peptide.Rd

Function write a script that can be used in pymol to color structure. Number of colors and corresponding to them ranges can be defined by user.

Usage

pymol_script_significant_peptide(
  df,
  path = "",
  ranges = c(-Inf, seq(-30, 30, by = 10), Inf),
  alpha = 0.01,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  replicates = 3,
  order.pep = TRUE,
  p_adjust = "none",
  resno_offset = 0,
  pv_cutoff
)

Arguments

df

output from functions output_tp

path

location where the scripts will be saved. Default "": the working directory.

ranges

ranges for coloring scheme. Default set to c(-Inf, seq(-30, 30, by=10), Inf)

alpha

cutoff for critical interval

pvalue

p-value cutoff here set up to 0.01

replicates

number of replicates in sample. Default set to 3.

order.pep

flag allowing to either order peptide acccording to the peptide length (default), or to position in the protein sequence.

p_adjust

multiple-testing correction of the Welch p-values, passed to stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default, raw p-values) or e.g. "BH". A peptide is significant when its (adjusted) p-value is below the cutoff AND its difference exceeds the critical interval.

resno_offset

integer added to every residue number written to the PyMOL script, so the data's numbering matches the structure's (e.g. -20 when the structure numbering starts 20 residues later, as with an N-terminal tag). Default 0.

pv_cutoff

deprecated, use pvalue.

Value

pymol script with colors assigned per peptide

Examples

# \donttest{
file_nm<-system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a<- output_tp(file_nm)
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written
pymol_script_significant_peptide(df=a, replicates=3, path=tempdir(),
alpha=0.01, pvalue=0.01,
ranges=c(-Inf,-40, -30,-20,-10, 0,10, 20,30,40, Inf), order.pep=TRUE )
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length

#> NULL
pymol_script_significant_peptide(df=a, path=tempdir())
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length
#> peptides ordered according to peptide length

#> NULL
# }
